iut_type: End Product (Toytec Bluetooth module), USB-UART level converter cable length constraint near the certification test system
customer_question: We have a KKHMF CH340 USB-UART module already on hand -- can we use it extended to over 1 meter, as shown in our attached setup diagram, since that's the distance needed between the test system's control PC and the test sample?
question_variants: Would a different, possibly cheaper level-converter board work as a substitute for the recommended one?
Is RF tester hardware something the customer needs to provide, or does the lab supply it?
actual_issue: The customer needed to confirm whether their already-on-hand USB-UART converter module could be used with an extension cable over 1 meter long to bridge the required distance between the certification test system's control PC and the test sample, and separately asked whether a different candidate level-converter board would work and whether RF test hardware was the customer's or the lab's responsibility.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG certification testing uses a SIG-certified test system supplied and operated by the lab (BQTF) itself -- not a general-purpose RF tester the customer would need to provide, and in Japan only three such certified systems exist. Extending the UART signal side of the connection beyond about 10-20cm is not recommended due to increased noise susceptibility at that signal level; instead, the test system side (the USB connection) should be extended using a shielded USB extension cable to bridge the roughly 1-meter gap, while the UART-to-DUT connection itself stays short. For the customer's candidate level-converter board, while not unsuitable, the lab recommended a specific alternative USB-UART adapter, since its cable length was sufficient for the full distance needed and it had a faster expected delivery time than the customer's candidate board, despite a similarly low cost (around ¥400).
consultant_answer: The certification test system is a SIG-certified system that we provide and operate ourselves -- not something you need to supply (there are only three such systems running in Japan). On the cabling: extending the UART side beyond about 10-20cm isn't recommended due to noise sensitivity at that signal level; instead, we'll extend the USB side using a shielded USB extension cable to cover the roughly 1-meter gap, keeping the UART-to-DUT run short. Your candidate level-converter board isn't unsuitable, but we'd recommend a specific alternative USB-UART adapter instead -- it has sufficient cable length for the full distance and a faster delivery time, at a similarly low cost (~¥400).
decision_logic: When extending a UART-based DUT connection to a certification test system over a meter or more, extend on the USB side (using a shielded USB extension cable) rather than the UART signal side, since UART is more noise-sensitive over longer cable runs -- and when a customer proposes a specific adapter, weigh it against alternatives on cable length sufficiency and delivery time, not just unit cost.
final_recommendation: When a customer proposes their own cabling/adapter hardware for a test setup, evaluate it against the test system's actual distance and noise-sensitivity requirements rather than approving or rejecting it on cost alone, and clarify upfront that the certification test system itself is lab-provided, not something the customer needs to supply.
risk_if_done_wrong: Extending the UART signal path beyond the recommended short distance could introduce noise-related connection instability during testing, while using an inadequate cable-length adapter could fail to physically bridge the required distance to the test system.
